findings.issue_text: [High/security] app/models/post.rb:131 — The `raw_html` cook method returns `raw` verbatim, completely bypassing Discourse's cooking/sanitization pipeline, and imported content is later rendered with `raw post.cooked`; any HTML pulled from the RSS feed or a remote page (script tags, event handlers, `javascript:` hrefs — readability only whitelists tags/attrs, it doesn't sanitize schemes) is stored as live markup that executes on the Discourse origin for every user who views the topic. Imported remote content must be run through the normal Sanitize pipeline before being stored in `cooked`.

[High/bug] app/views/embed/best.html.erb:9 — `<%- end if %>` is not valid Ruby once the template is compiled (ERB/erubis terminate `<% %>` chunks with `;`, producing `end if ;`, a syntax error), so `best.html.erb` fails to compile and /embed/best 500s whenever a topic exists; even under newline-preserving engines it only parses by accidentally consuming the next ERB chunk as the if modifier's condition. Should be `<%- end %>`. The controller specs never render views, so this is untested.

[Medium/security] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` un-escapes the feed item's content before storing it as raw HTML; even a well-behaved feed that safely escapes markup (e.g., `<script>` in a description) has its escaping undone, converting it into executable HTML that is then stored un-sanitized via the raw_html cook path.

[Medium/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `url` is interpolated unescaped into the `embed.imported_from` anchor (`#{url}`); the only gate is the `^https?\://` regex and in the poll_feed path (`i.link`) the value is never URI-parsed, so a link like `http://x/'>

[Medium/security] lib/topic_retriever.rb:17 / app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — The embeddable-host check (`URI(@embed_url).host == embeddable_host`) applies only to the initial URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects, so content from any host (including internal network hosts — an SSRF read primitive, since the extracted text lands in a public topic) can be imported and stored as raw HTML.

[Medium/security] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:18 — The postMessage origin check uses substring containment (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`) instead of exact origin equality, so any origin whose string appears as a prefix/substring of `discourseUrl` (e.g., the parent domain for subpath installs) can drive the handler; `e.data.height` is also used unvalidated. Compare `e.origin` exactly against the expected origin and coerce/validate height as a number.

[Medium/performance] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every unauthenticated GET /embed/best with an un-imported `embed_url` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job with no endpoint-level rate limit (the 60s redis throttle is per-URL, so unique URLs bypass it), and each job may re-fetch and parse the entire RSS feed inline (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` in topic_retriever.rb:39) plus the remote page; the Referer guard is trivially spoofed off-browser, making this a sidekiq/outbound-HTTP amplification vector.

[Medium/bug] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:22-32 — There is no error handling anywhere in the poll chain: a transient fetch failure, a feed item missing `content`/`title` (`nil.scrub`/nil title into PostCreator), or an import exception aborts the whole item loop; with `retry: false`, nothing is retried until the next hourly run and all items after the failing one are never imported.

[Medium/bug] app/models/topic_embed.rb:61,67 — `absolutize_urls` rewrites any href/src that `start_with?('/')`, which includes protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.host/img.png`); these get mangled into `http://<embeddable-host>/cdn.host/img.png`, silently breaking links/images in imported content. The check must exclude `//` prefixes.

[Medium/data] db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Unrelated modification of an already-shipped migration adds `force: true`, which will silently DROP the existing `top_topics` table and its data if the migration is ever re-run (redo/reset/migrate against a DB where the version isn't recorded); modifying released migrations (and the whitespace-only churn in 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb) is also out of scope for this PR.

[Medium/test_gap] spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb — Only the site-setting guards are tested; poll_feed's actual behavior (feed fetch/parse, link→id fallback, content extraction, `TopicEmbed.import` invocation, error handling) has zero coverage, and the spec requires an unrelated job (`require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` — copy-paste from process_post's spec).

[Low/bug] app/models/topic_embed.rb:34,37 — The update path assumes `embed.post` is present; if the first post was deleted (the TopicEmbed row survives), `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises NoMethodError, which — combined with the lack of error handling in the poll loop — permanently breaks the hourly feed poll for that feed.

[Low/concurrency] lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 — `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire` is not atomic; a crash between the two leaves the `retrieved:<url>` key with no TTL, so that embed_url is treated as 'recently retrieved' forever and never imported (the embed stays stuck on the loading view). Use a single `SET key 1 EX 60 NX`.

[Low/security] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26 — `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open`, which executes shell commands for values beginning with `|` (classic open-uri pitfall); admin-only input today, but it should go through `URI(...)` + OpenURI (or a proper HTTP client) to be safe.
[Low/bug] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:18-20 — `feed_key` is dead code: it is computed but never called, so the intended feed-modified caching/short-circuit was never wired up.

[Low/data] lib/tasks/disqus.thor:141-144 — The rework drops `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, so imported Disqus threads are stamped with the current time instead of their original dates, and the removed `--category/-c` option breaks existing import invocations — unrelated regressions bundled into this PR.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] app/models/post.rb:131 — The `raw_html` cook method returns `raw` verbatim, completely bypassing Discourse's cooking/sanitization pipeline, and imported content is later rendered with `raw post.cooked`; any HTML pulled from the RSS feed or a remote page (script tags, event handlers, `javascript:` hrefs — readability only whitelists tags/attrs, it doesn't sanitize schemes) is stored as live markup that executes on the Discourse origin for every user who views the topic. adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using HTML from feeds/remote pages (`SimpleRSS.parse ... i.content` in Jobs::PollFeed; `Readability::Document ... doc.content` in TopicEmbed.import_remote) without passing through Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization. The embed view renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any unsafe markup in imported content would execute in the Discourse origin. The diff does not show any sanitization of the imported HTML before storing/rendering, making the XSS concern directly grounded in the changes.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed item content is transformed with `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passed into `TopicEmbed.import`. That method persists it via `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], skip_validations: true)`. With `cook_method == :raw_html`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders it using `raw post.cooked`. Therefore, unescaping entities (e.g. `<script>`) can indeed turn previously escaped markup into executable HTML that is stored and later rendered unsanitized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] lib/topic_retriever.rb:17 / app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — The embeddable-host check (`URI(@embed_url).host == embeddable_host`) applies only to the initial URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects, so content from any host (including internal network hosts — an SSRF read primitive, since the extracted text lands in a public topic) can be imported and stored as raw HTML.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` the host allowlist check is performed only against the initially provided `@embed_url` (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). However, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` then calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (open-uri). The diff shows no verification of the final URL after redirects, nor any restriction on redirect hosts, so a URL on the allowed host can redirect to a different host (including internal network addresses) and have its content imported. The imported content is then stored into a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for that method, so the fetched content is persisted and rendered without the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. This matches the finding’s SSRF + unsafe import concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every unauthenticated GET /embed/best with an un-imported `embed_url` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job with no endpoint-level rate limit (the 60s redis throttle is per-URL, so unique URLs bypass it), and each job may re-fetch and parse the entire RSS feed inline (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` in topic_retriever.rb:39) plus the remote page; the Referer guard is trivially spoofed off-browser, making this a sidekiq/outbound-HTTP amplification vector.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unauthenticated `GET /embed/best` endpoint that, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The job calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, whose throttle is keyed by the full URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so many unique URLs on the allowed host bypass the 60s throttle (lib/topic_retriever.rb). For each new URL, `perform_retrieve` may synchronously run `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (which fetches/parses the entire feed via `open` + `SimpleRSS.parse`) and then fetch the remote page via `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, app/models/topic_embed.rb). The controller's Referer check is the only gate and is header-spoofable by non-browser clients, making this a plausible Sidekiq/outbound-HTTP amplification/DoS vector introduced by the change.

Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.host/img.png` also satisfy this and will be transformed via `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` into `cdn.host/img.png`, then prefixed with the article host (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.host/img.png`), which is incorrect and breaks those links/images.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Unrelated modification of an already-shipped migration adds `force: true`, which will silently DROP the existing `top_topics` table and its data if the migration is ever re-run (redo/reset/migrate against a DB where the version isn't recorded); modifying released migrations (and the whitespace-only churn in 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb) is also out of scope for this PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3). In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists, so if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., rollback/redo, reset, or a DB where the version isn’t recorded but the table exists), it can silently destroy `top_topics` data. The diff also shows unrelated whitespace-only edits in 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb, supporting the “out of scope” portion of the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb — Only the site-setting guards are tested; poll_feed's actual behavior (feed fetch/parse, link→id fallback, content extraction, `TopicEmbed.import` invocation, error handling) has zero coverage, and the spec requires an unrelated job (`require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` — copy-paste from process_post's spec).

adjudication.rationale: The new job `Jobs::PollFeed` contains nontrivial logic in `poll_feed` (requires `simple-rss`, `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, iterates `rss.items`, falls back `url = i.id` when `i.link` is blank/invalid, extracts `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and calls `TopicEmbed.import`). The added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts the site-setting preconditions and that `poll_feed` is (not) called from `execute`, and does not cover `poll_feed` behavior at all. Additionally, the spec includes `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`, which is unrelated to `PollFeed` and appears to be copy/paste. This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage issue, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/models/topic_embed.rb:34,37 — The update path assumes `embed.post` is present; if the first post was deleted (the TopicEmbed row survives), `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises NoMethodError, which — combined with the lack of error handling in the poll loop — permanently breaks the hourly feed poll for that feed.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the SHA changes (app/models/topic_embed.rb around the `else` branch). Since there are no foreign keys and no `dependent:` behavior shown, a `topic_embeds` row can survive after its referenced `posts` row is deleted, making `embed.post` nil and causing a NoMethodError inside `PostRevisor`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` with no rescue, so such an exception would abort the poll run and would likely repeat on subsequent hourly runs until the orphan is cleaned up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 — `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire` is not atomic; a crash between the two leaves the `retrieved:<url>` key with no TTL, so that embed_url is treated as 'recently retrieved' forever and never imported (the embed stays stuck on the loading view). Use a single `SET key 1 EX 60 NX`.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `retrieved_recently?` uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key can be left without a TTL. On later calls `setnx` will fail and the method will return `true` (treated as “retrieved recently”) forever, preventing `perform_retrieve` from running and leaving embeds stuck loading. Using an atomic `SET ... NX EX 60` would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26 — `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open`, which executes shell commands for values beginning with `|` (classic open-uri pitfall); admin-only input today, but it should go through `URI(...)` + OpenURI (or a proper HTTP client) to be safe.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, the code does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` after requiring `open-uri`. This uses `Kernel#open` (patched by open-uri), which in classic Ruby can treat strings beginning with `|` as a command to execute, making it a command-injection risk if the setting is ever set to such a value. The finding accurately describes this open-uri pitfall and is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:18-20 — `feed_key` is dead code: it is computed but never called, so the intended feed-modified caching/short-circuit was never wired up.

adjudication.rationale: In the added Jobs::PollFeed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), the method `feed_key` is defined (lines ~18-20 in the new file) but is never referenced anywhere in this diff (no call in `execute`/`poll_feed` or elsewhere). That makes it verifiable dead code. However, this does not create broken behavior by itself; it suggests an unfinished/unused caching/throttling feature rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] lib/tasks/disqus.thor:141-144 — The rework drops `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, so imported Disqus threads are stamped with the current time instead of their original dates, and the removed `--category/-c` option breaks existing import invocations — unrelated regressions bundled into this PR.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the PR removes the `--category/-c` Thor option (deleted `method_option :category`) and all logic that maps it to a category_id, so existing invocations using `-c/--category` will fail. It also replaces the PostCreator call that set `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and neither `import_remote` nor `TopicEmbed.import` pass a `created_at` option into `PostCreator`, so imported threads/posts will default to current timestamps instead of original Disqus dates.
